title: Weakening approximation thresholds
statement: Let $A$ be a polynomial-time map for an encoded maximization problem, and suppose that on every well-formed instance its output is feasible and, whenever the optimum is at least $q$, its output value is at least $r$. If $r'\le r$ and $q\le q'$, then on every well-formed instance the output is feasible and, whenever the optimum is at least $q'$, its output value is at least $r'$.
hypotheses_covered: The encoded maximization problem has a well-formed instance language, feasibility relation, objective value, and stated optimum
$A$’s output is feasible on every well-formed instance
If the optimum is at least $q$, the output value is at least $r$
